subproblem.title: Lower mass bound for an integer multiplicity current: ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) for open W
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and R = (C, θ, ξ) an IMRep in U with R.Represents T. Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, R.measure W = (θ Hⁿ⌞C)(W) ≤ M_W(T) = T.massOn W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → R.measure W ≤ T.massOn W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 3 of the parent node's supplied proof of the mass formula M_W(T) = R.measure W (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3)). Notation: C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ_C := μHE[n].restrict C, μ := R.measure = μ_C.withDensity θ, |·|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm. Sibling lemmas used: regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing ((i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E, (ii) ∃ β, |β|_E ≤ 1 ∧ ξ(x)(β) = 1, whenever IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q), regcomp_covector_field_near_maximizer and regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx (statements as frozen).

1. (Consequences of the orientation condition.) By R.orients and regcomp_unit_orientation_pairing, for μ_C-a.e. x: (i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α, and (ii) there is β with |β|_E ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1.

2. (Reduction to W' := W ∩ U.) W' is open. μ(Uᶜ) = 0: μ ≪ μ_C (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous) and μ_C(Uᶜ) = μHE[n](Uᶜ ∩ C) = 0 since C ⊆ U (R.carrier_subset). Hence μ(W) ≤ μ(W') + μ(Uᶜ) = μ(W') (measure_mono, measure_union_le). It therefore suffices to show c ≤ T.massOn W for every c ∈ ℝ≥0∞ with c < μ(W') (then μ(W') ≤ T.massOn W by le_of_forall_lt).

3. (Compact exhaustion.) Fix c < μ(W'). There are compact sets K_0 ⊆ K_1 ⊆ ⋯ with ⋃_j K_j = W': if W' = ℝ^P take K_j := closedBall(0, j); otherwise let d(z) := infDist z W'ᶜ (continuous, and d(z) > 0 iff z ∈ W' because W'ᶜ is closed and nonempty: IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos) and take K_j := closedBall(0, j) ∩ {z : 1/(j + 1) ≤ d(z)} (closed and bounded, hence compact in the proper space ℝ^P; contained in W'; increasing; every z ∈ W' lies in K_j for j large). [Equivalently: IsOpen.exists_iUnion_isClosed gives closed F_j increasing to W'; take K_j := F_j ∩ closedBall(0, j).] By continuity of μ from below (tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop), μ(K_j) → μ(W'), so there is a compact K ⊆ W' with c < μ(K).

4. (Open neighbourhood with finite measure.) By exists_compact_between choose a compact L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ W'; put O := interior L. Then O is open and K ⊆ O ⊆ L ⊆ W' ⊆ W ∩ U. Moreover μ(L) = ∫⁻_L θ dμ_C = ∫⁻_{C ∩ L} θ dμHE[n] < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, and R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set L ⊆ U). Hence μ(K) ≤ μ(O) ≤ μ(L) < ∞ and ν := μ.restrict O is a finite measure. Put m := μ(K).toReal, so μ(K) = ofReal m and c < ofReal m.

5. (Fix η ∈ (0, 1): near-maximizing field.) By 1(ii) and R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient, regcomp_covector_field_near_maximizer applied to μ_C, ξ and η yields a strongly measurable g₀ with |g₀(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x and 1 − η ≤ ξ(x)(g₀(x)) for μ_C-a.e. x. Put g := K.indicator g₀: strongly measurable (K is closed, StronglyMeasurable.indicator), |g(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x (|0|_E = 0), and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

6. (Lower bound for the model integral.) Let F(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)). F is μ_C-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable; x ↦ ξ(x)(g(x)) is the continuous evaluation map applied to the a.e. strongly measurable pair (ξ, g)), and by 1(i) |F| ≤ θ·1_K μ_C-a.e.; since ∫⁻ θ·1_K dμ_C = μ(K) < ∞, F is μ_C-integrable. μ_C-a.e. F ≥ (1 − η)·θ·1_K (on K by step 5, off K both sides vanish). Hence ∫ F dμ_C ≥ (1 − η)·∫ θ·1_K dμ_C = (1 − η)·m (integral_mono_ae; integral of the nonnegative function θ·1_K equals (∫⁻ θ·1_K dμ_C).toReal = μ(K).toReal).

7. (Smooth admissible form.) Apply regcomp_exists_smooth_unit_form_approx to ν, O, K, g (ν finite, O open, K compact, K ⊆ O, g strongly measurable, |g|_E ≤ 1, g = 0 off K) and ε := η: there is h with IsTestForm h, tsupport h ⊆ O, |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z and ∫⁻ ofReal|h − g|_E dν < ofReal η. Since tsupport h ⊆ O ⊆ U, ω := ⟨h, IsTestForm h, tsupport h ⊆ U⟩ ∈ TestFormOn U n, and ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W because tsupport h ⊆ O ⊆ W and |h|_E ≤ 1. Hence ofReal(T ω) ≤ T.massOn W (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).

8. (Comparison.) By R.Represents T, T ω = R.action h = ∫ θ ξ(h) dμ_C. The integrand is μ_C-integrable: a.e. strongly measurable, and |θ ξ(h)| ≤ θ·1_{tsupport h} a.e. by 1(i) and |h|_E ≤ 1, with ∫⁻_{C ∩ tsupport h} θ dμHE[n] < ∞ (tsupport h is compact and ⊆ U; R.locallyIntegrable_mult). By linearity of ξ(x), T ω − ∫ F dμ_C = ∫ θ·ξ(h − g) dμ_C (integral_sub, map_sub). Then ofReal|T ω − ∫ F dμ_C| ≤ ∫⁻ ‖θ·ξ(h − g)‖ₑ dμ_C (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm) ≤ ∫⁻ θ·ofReal|h − g|_E dμ_C (1(i)) = ∫⁻ ofReal|h − g|_E dμ (lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀; θ is measurable, and x ↦ ofReal|h(x) − g(x)|_E is measurable because h is continuous, g is strongly measurable and covectorEuclideanNorm is continuous, being the square root of a finite sum of squares of the continuous linear evaluations α ↦ α(e∘I)) = ∫⁻ ofReal|h − g|_E dν (the integrand vanishes off O, since h = 0 off tsupport h ⊆ O and g = 0 off K ⊆ O) < ofReal η. Hence |T ω − ∫ F dμ_C| < η and, by step 6, T ω > (1 − η)m − η.

9. (Letting η ↓ 0.) Steps 5–8 give ofReal((1 − η)m − η) ≤ T.massOn W for every η ∈ (0, 1). If T.massOn W < ofReal m, then T.massOn W = ofReal a with a := (T.massOn W).toReal < m, and choosing η ∈ (0, 1) with (1 − η)m − η > a (possible since (1 − η)m − η → m as η → 0) gives a contradiction. Hence c < μ(K) = ofReal m ≤ T.massOn W.

10. (Conclusion.) As c < μ(W') was arbitrary, μ(W') ≤ T.massOn W, and by step 2, R.measure W = μ(W) ≤ μ(W') ≤ T.massOn W. ∎
proof_key_steps: A.e. on C, ξ(x) has dual coefficient norm 1 (unit orientation pairing); μ(W) = μ(W ∩ U).
Inner approximation of W' = W ∩ U by compact K with μ(K) > c, and an open O with K ⊆ O ⊆ L ⊆ W' (L compact), so μ⌞O is finite.
Near-maximizing measurable field g = 1_K g₀ gives ∫ θ ξ(g) dHⁿ⌞C ≥ (1 − η) μ(K).
Smooth admissible h supported in O with ∫ |h − g|_E d(μ⌞O) < η gives T(h) > (1 − η) μ(K) − η.

audit.reason: Reduction to W ∩ U, compact exhaustion, and local integrability provide the finite neighborhood measure required by the analytic children. The proof verifies their hypotheses, integrability of both action terms, and the withDensity error conversion. Letting η decrease to zero and exhausting compact masses proves the exact lower bound, including infinite mass.
